To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

vitamin K-dependent proteins are widely distributed throughout the animal and vegetable kingdom, that vitamin K-dependent protein synthesis is not limited to a specific tissue, that vitamin K is a substrate for the enzyme, that vitamin K epoxide and vitamin K 2,3-epoxide are inhibitors of the enzyme, that the enzyme has a high affinity for vitamin K, that the enzyme is inhibited by vitamin K epoxide, that the enzyme requires O2, that the enzyme contains a flavin cofactor, that the

vitamin K-dependent protein carboxylase, which is a micrososomal enzyme, can be found in many different tissues, and that there are differences between the substrate-binding site of various carboxylation enzymes.
vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation of glutamic acid residues is a microsomed enzyme reaction that is catalyzed by a family of isozymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of vitamin K-dependent carboxesylation reactions in various tissues.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of the enzyme system involved in vitamin K-dependent carboxesylation of proteins.
the elucidation of the mechanism of the vitamin K-dependent car-boxylase reaction and the identification of its substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vitamin K-dependent protein carboxylase exists in different forms in different tissues.

the vitamin K-dependent carboxesylation reaction is catalysed by an isoenzyme system which is widely distributed throughout the body and which has a common vitamin K-binding site, but a different Gla-protein-binding site in each isoenzyme.
the carboxylase from liver is different from the carboxylases in bone and testis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin K-dependent proteins are not only widely distributed but that the carboxylation process is also widely distributed.
the vitamin K-dependent car boxylase is a family of microsomal enzymes that are present in all types of tissue.
vitamin K-dependent protein carboxylation is an essential step in the biosynthesis of a large number of biologically active proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a family of vitamin K-dependent carboxesylases, each of which carboxylates a different set of Gla-containing proteins.
vitamin K is not the only factor determining the specificity of carboxylases.
the substrate-binding sites of the different vitamin K-dependent carboxesylase isoforms are different.
